not_costed.name: PaddleOCR
not_costed.why: accurate (recall 0.73) but 25.6 s/frame on one CPU process; per-instance parallelism not measured

not_costed.name: Tesseract
not_costed.why: recall 0.18 and precision 0.41 on our frames

assumptions: 1 frame per second, as measured. Sampling every 2 s would halve every figure here and cost recall on short appearances (not measured).
Apple options assume an EC2 Mac M4 host matches the speed of the machine we measured on. That is not tested.
Hosts are on-demand at $1.23 per host-hour with a 24-hour minimum, so small batches pay for a full day per host.
Recall is pooled over 156 hand-labelled frames (176 boards) from three highlight edits. Full matches have more wide shots.
Cloud-API figures are list prices with no volume discount or committed-use deal.

stages.stage: Break the video into frames (ffmpeg, 1 per second)
Read every frame: full frame, 6 zoomed tiles, Chinese pass (Apple Vision, 8 workers)
Match text to brands and total the seconds

optional.stage: Google Video Intelligence logo recognition (optional, runs in Google's cloud)
optional.note: about 6 min upload plus about 55 min processing, measured on one 104-minute match

not_included: Human review of detections (precision audit, recall labels): not timed, not costed
Moving the video into AWS and storing it: not priced
A 24-hour minimum applies to every EC2 Mac host, so a host must stay busy for the per-hour figures to hold

quality_definition: mean of the share of all boards found and the share of small boards found, on the 156 labelled frames
